title: Client toggle hushplan and rollback notes
body:
Goal:
- Lightweight, client-driven safe ramp for toggling model variants via SDK flags. Keep changes reversible with a single command and minimal blast radius.

Context / motivation:
- We want to let a small slice of customers hit the new kv-cache-friendly quantized variant (q4_0) while keeping default traffic on stable.
- Some clients will flip via SDK feature flags; others via server-side routing. This doc is about the SDK path (device->SDK->api).
- Prior incidents: 2025-11 small memory spike when warmup missing; need to ensure warmup cohort and client throttles.

Assumptions:
- Client SDK supports per-client feature flag with TTL and sticky session (client-side cookie + server fallback).
- We can push a forced kill-switch from Console to override client toggles.
- Telemetry: per-client latency, error-rate, token-cost, cache-hit-ratio are available in 30s buckets.

Safe toggle flow (recommended):
1) Preflight (local): sanity run with sample prompts, verify model name & checksum, ensure kv-cache warming completed.
2) Canary cohort (1% of clients): flip SDK flag for cohort A for 30 minutes. Monitor signals below.
3) Gradual doubling every 30m: 1% -> 2% -> 4% -> 8% -> 16% -> stop/evaluate.
4) If at any stage a threshold is breached, revert flag for last cohort and hold for 30m.
5) After 4x stable increments, if no regressions, schedule a broad ramp to 50% then 100% with longer observation windows.

Preflight checklist (quick):
- [ ] Confirm model artifact id and quantization profile (artifact: q4_0-2026-03-08-sha256:abcd1234)
- [ ] Update SDK rollout config in feature service (config id: sdk-rollout-2026-03-10)
- [ ] Create canary cohort key (cohort: sdk-canary-a)
- [ ] Create monitoring dashboard (tilt: SDK Toggle - q4_0 canary)
- [ ] Reserve on-call (eng-release) for rollout window + 2 hours after
- [ ] Add quick rollback runbook link to the dashboard

Rollout window constraints:
- Prefer quiet hours in EU morning / US evening (UTC 18:00-02:00) to reduce production churn and allow EMEA/APAC observation.
- Avoid major customer demos, marketing pushes, or infra maintenance windows.
- For large customers on dedicated capacity, coordinate with Customer Success.

Monitoring signals and thresholds (auto-alerts):
- 5m error-rate increase > 0.5pp absolute or > 2x baseline -> SEV-2 alert to oncall
- 1m P95 latency increase > 250ms absolute -> SEV-2
- Token-cost-per-request increase > 15% -> ops review (cost regression)
- Cache-hit-ratio drop > 10pp -> likely warmup issue
- OOMs or host GPU memory warnings -> immediate rollback (SEV-1)
- Any upstream client SDK exceptions (parsing, handshake) >= 3/min for cohort -> rollback

Fast rollback commands (SDK/Console):
- Console override (preferred): go to Console -> Feature flags -> sdk-rollout-2026-03-10 -> set global=off.
- API (admin):
  curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/admin/flags/sdks/sdk-rollout-2026-03-10/override" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"state":"off","note":"fast rollback - operator"}'
  (replace $ADMIN)
- SDK-side: push ephemeral TTL=0 to clients via pubsub topic: "sdk-config-refresh" with payload {"sdk-rollout-2026-03-10": "off"} (ops only)

Post-rollback wants:
- Collect 30m logs for the cohort (trace sampling 100% for affected clients)
- Run quick diff on prompt outputs vs baseline for 50 sampled requests
- Open incident note in runbook and ping product + cs if customer-visible

Observability quick-map (where to look):
- Dashboards: /dashboards/sdk-toggle-q4_0-canary
- Traces: service=client-sdk, tag=feature:sdk-rollout-2026-03-10
- Errors: logs index "client-sdk-errors"
- Cost: /billing/token-unit-breakdown filtered by model=q4_0

Edge cases / gotchas:
- Mobile SDKs may cache flag state; ensure TTL and Jitter to reduce synchronized flips.
- Some clients pre-warm by sending synthetic prompts; this can skew cache-hit metrics. Add label synthetic=true when applicable.
- For long-lived sessions, toggles may not apply until new session handshake; consider forcing session-reconnect for canary cohort if safe.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we need to bump JWT lifetime for canary clients to avoid auth refresh interruption? (TBD with infra)
- Add automatic warmup injector that runs top-50 prompts for cohort seed: ticket RDEV-4217.
- Decide whether to enable local client-side telemetry opt-in for canary cohorts (privacy implications).

Notes to self:
- Keep the first canary small and watch cache-hit-ratio early (within 2-3 minutes). Warmup failures show up as increased latency + cost.
- If we see slow memory growth but stable errors, consider throttling request rate rather than immediate rollback to gather better signals.
- Remember to annotate the rollout in the product calendar and customer-facing changelog if we push beyond 25%.

Quick reference: rollback one-liners:
- Admin API override: curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/admin/flags/sdks/sdk-rollout-2026-03-10/override" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"state":"off"}'
- Console path: Console > Feature flags > sdk-rollout-2026-03-10 > Override -> off

End of notes.

-- kai
(revisit after first canary run, annotate timestamps and reactions)
